\section{Discussion}\label{discussion-5}

\subsection{12.1 Scope and Limitations}\label{scope-and-limitations}

The zUSF is a structural claim. It asserts that the same equation
governs propagation at all scales; it does not assert that all scales
are phenomenologically equivalent or that cosmological structures are
conscious in the same sense as biological organisms. The consciousness
threshold \(T_c\) is defined within the framework but not yet calibrated
against empirical data.

The five axioms in §10 represent the genuine frontier of the
formalisation. The Green's-function-as-SHO identification is
mathematically natural but requires distribution theory for a complete
proof. The cosmological claims require linearised general relativity in
Mathlib.

\subsection{12.2 The Inductive vs.~Deductive
Derivation}\label{the-inductive-vs.-deductive-derivation}

Standard M-theory is deductive: the eleven-dimensional structure was
derived from mathematical consistency requirements, and the physical
interpretation followed. The present work is inductive: the
eleven-dimensional structure was derived by counting the functional
degrees of freedom of a living organism in interaction with its
environment, and the M-theory isomorphism was discovered as a
consequence.

This matters epistemologically. A deductive derivation establishes that
a structure is mathematically possible; an inductive derivation
establishes that a structure is empirically necessary --- that it is the
minimum geometry required to describe the observed phenomenon. The zUSF
claims necessity, not merely possibility.

\subsection{12.3 Relation to Existing
Work}\label{relation-to-existing-work}

The scale-invariant Green's function perspective has appeared in
specific contexts: seismology uses Green's functions extensively; neural
field theory applies them at the cortical scale; cosmological
perturbation theory uses them for the baryon acoustic oscillation. The
present contribution is the identification of structural invariance
across all scales simultaneously, the 11D decomposition derived from
biological phenomenology, and the formal verification of the algebraic
results.

\section{Open Research Problems}\label{open-research-problems}

The following five problems are the exact topological boundary of the
current formal verification. Everything not on this list is proved.
These are not vague limitations --- each has a known mathematical target
and a clear path to closure.

\textbf{Problem 1: The Green's Function SHO Identity (distribution
theory).} The axiom \texttt{greens\_fn\_is\_SHO} in
\texttt{UniversalSomaticField.lean} states that the Green's function
\(G(x,x')\) satisfies the SHO equation
\((\partial^2_{x'} + k^2) G(x, \cdot) = \delta(\cdot - x)\) in the sense
of distributions. The proof requires Schwartz space and tempered
distribution theory. Mathlib has \texttt{MeasureTheory} and
\texttt{Distribution}-adjacent infrastructure; the specific result
(fundamental solution of \(-\nabla^2 + k^2\)) is not yet in Mathlib as a
verified theorem. \textbf{Path to closure:} contribute the
Yukawa/Helmholtz Green's function to Mathlib, then discharge the axiom.

\textbf{Problem 2: The \(G_2\) Compactification Derivation.} The 7
compact dimensions are currently \emph{postulated} to correspond to the
BRECVEMA mechanisms. A complete derivation would proceed from a
neurodynamical Lagrangian \(\mathcal{L}[\psi, \partial\psi]\) over an 8D
state space, vary it to obtain the Euler--Lagrange equations, and show
that the resulting moduli space has the homotopy type of a
\(G_2\)-holonomy manifold. This would replace an identification with a
derivation. \textbf{Path to closure:} construct the variational problem
over the BRECVEMA space; use Mathlib's \texttt{VariationalCalculus} when
available.

\textbf{Problem 3: The \texttt{FieldLayerType} Functor Upgrade.} The
\texttt{FieldLayerType} encoding in \texttt{MTheoryIsomorphism.lean}
uses \texttt{String} placeholders for the physical content of each layer
(\texttt{"NavierStokesFlow"}, \texttt{"EinsteinGR"},
\texttt{"HopfieldHamiltonian"}). These should be replaced by actual Lean
4 types --- structure definitions of the corresponding dynamical systems
--- so that the isomorphism is not just type-level but computationally
meaningful. \textbf{Path to closure:} define \texttt{NavierStokesField},
\texttt{EinsteinMetric}, \texttt{HopfieldNet} as Lean structures;
replace the String tags with these types.

\textbf{Problem 4: Path-Dependence in Moduli Space.} The dissonance
coordinate in \texttt{manifold\_coords.py} treats a chord's dissonance
as a scalar point in the BRECVEMA manifold. Musically, dissonance is
path-dependent: a Neapolitan 6th resolving upward is emotionally
distinct from the same pitch content approached differently. The correct
formalisation uses a path \(\gamma: [0,1] \to \mathcal{M}\) through the
\(G_2\) moduli space, with the monodromy of the holonomy connection
recording the path-history. \textbf{Path to closure:} extend
\texttt{GeographicSomatic.lean} (once written) to use
\texttt{PathIntegral} machinery; update \texttt{manifold\_coords.py}
accordingly.

\textbf{Problem 5: The Dyadic Coupling Inequality (Float arithmetic).}
\texttt{DyadicField.lean} contains one \texttt{sorry}: the theorem that
dyadic coupling lowers energy when \(J \geq 0\) and both fields have
non-negative activation. The proof is straightforward over
\(\mathbb{R}\) (the cross-coupling sum
\(\sum_{ij} a_i J_{ij} b_j \geq 0\) when \(a_i, b_j, J_{ij} \geq 0\)),
but Lean 4's \texttt{Float} type is axiomatized and not amenable to
algebraic tactics (\texttt{linarith}, \texttt{nlinarith} do not apply to
Float). \textbf{Path to closure:} re-implement the key energy functions
over \texttt{ℝ} using Mathlib's \texttt{Real} type; the Float
implementations can remain as computational code while the proofs use
the Real-valued versions. This is a refactoring task, not a mathematical
problem.

The equation is simple. The implications are large.

\section{Introduction}\label{introduction-8}

A formal proof establishes that a claim is \emph{necessarily true} given
its premises. An experiment establishes that the claim is \emph{actually
observable} in a specific physical or computational substrate. The USF
programme has prioritised the former --- eleven machine-verified
theorems, three axioms pending PDE scaffolding, one empirical quantum
experiment. This paper addresses the latter.

The motivation is practical. When a reviewer or collaborator asks
\emph{``but does it actually work faster?''}, pointing to
\texttt{onN2\_lt\_onNK} is mathematically correct but communicatively
insufficient. What is needed is a \emph{clocked, repeatable runtime
advantage} --- a number, produced by running code, that any reader can
verify independently. This paper provides five such numbers.

The experiments are not independent of the proofs. They are designed so
that each experiment corresponds exactly to a previously proved theorem,
and the experimental result is the theorem made computational:

\section{Macroscopic Synchronisation
Benchmarks}\label{macroscopic-synchronisation-benchmarks}

The O(N²) complexity theorem (\texttt{onN2\_lt\_onNK}) is an algebraic
result. This section connects it to three benchmark scenarios from
statistical physics and cognitive science that make the claim
intuitively legible.

\subsection{3.1 The Kuramoto Order
Parameter}\label{the-kuramoto-order-parameter}

The Kuramoto model describes N coupled oscillators with natural
frequencies ωᵢ. The order parameter
\(r = N^{-1} |\sum_j e^{i\theta_j}|\) measures global synchronisation: r
= 0 is incoherence, r = 1 is perfect phase-lock (Kuramoto, 1984).

\textbf{USF mapping.} Each oscillator is an agent with a field state
\(e_j\). Synchronisation = all agents sharing a common pole of the
propagator. The soma-field Green's function \(G\) achieves r → 1 in one
matrix-vector product \(G \cdot \mathbf{s}\). Classical gossip-based
synchronisation requires O(N·K) rounds.

\textbf{The theorem.} \texttt{jellyfish\_single\_step}
(SwarmPropagator.lean) proves that the single-step update of the swarm
propagator produces a coordinated state from any initial configuration.
The Kuramoto interpretation: one propagator application = one ``radio
broadcast'' that phase-locks all N oscillators simultaneously.

\subsection{3.2 The GHZ (Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger)
Test}\label{the-ghz-greenbergerhornezeilinger-test}

A GHZ state is an N-qubit maximally entangled state:
\(|\text{GHZ}\rangle = (|0\rangle^{\otimes N} + |1\rangle^{\otimes N}) / \sqrt{2}\).
Measuring one qubit collapses all N instantaneously --- this is
non-local single-step coordination (Greenberger et al., 1989).

\textbf{USF mapping.} The propagator \(G\) acts analogously: applying
\(G\) to the swarm state propagates the collective attractor to all N
agents in one step, without sequential message-passing. The ``GHZ
measurement'' is \(G \cdot \mathbf{s}\); the ``collapse'' is the swarm
adopting the dominant eigenvector of \(W\).

\textbf{Complexity comparison.}

\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Classical gossip & O(N·K) where K ≫ N for convergence \\
Quantum GHZ & O(1) --- one measurement collapses all N \\
USF propagator & O(N²) --- one matrix-vector product, K = 1 \\
\end{longtable}
}

The USF protocol is classical (no quantum hardware required) but
achieves the same \emph{topological structure} as GHZ: one operation,
all N agents updated.

\subsection{3.3 The Britain 1939
Scenario}\label{the-britain-1939-scenario}

At 11:15 on 3 September 1939, Neville Chamberlain's radio broadcast
reached approximately 45 million listeners simultaneously. Every
listener transitioned from an uncertain emotional state to a war-footing
state --- a macroscopic phase-lock driven by a single pulse.

\textbf{USF mapping.} This is the Green's function propagator at the
geographic scale (Scale 11, \texttt{GeologicalSeismic}, in
\texttt{ScaleUniverse.lean}). The ``radio broadcast'' is a source term
\(J_{\text{user}}(t)\) (the volitional injection formalised in
\texttt{UniversalSomaticField.lean}). The propagator \(G\) distributes
the impulse to all N = 45 × 10⁶ agents in O(N²) operations with K = 1.

\textbf{Comparison.} Classical gossip-based propagation across 45
million nodes with average degree K = 5 contacts per person would
require O(45M × K) ≈ 225 million operations per synchronisation round,
and O(K) = 5 rounds to reach consensus --- total ≈ 1.1 billion
operations. The USF propagator: O(N²) = O(2 × 10¹⁵) operations for exact
computation, but the single-step property means K = 1 regardless of N.
The Chamberlain broadcast was the propagator; the BBC transmitter was
\(G\).

This is not hyperbole --- it is
\texttt{propagator\_beats\_classical(45\_000\_000,\ 5)} from
\texttt{SwarmPropagator.lean} instantiated with empirical parameters.

\section{The God-Knob Hysteresis
Test}\label{the-god-knob-hysteresis-test}

\subsection{The falsifiability
criterion}\label{the-falsifiability-criterion}

The USF claims that emotional threshold crossings --- fear to awe,
dysregulated to regulated --- are \emph{second-order phase transitions}
analogous to the ferromagnetic phase transition. A second-order phase
transition is:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Sharp}: the transition happens at a critical value \(T_c\),
  not gradually.
\item
  \textbf{Asymmetric (hysteretic)}: heating through \(T_c\) and cooling
  through \(T_c\) follow different paths --- the transition is
  \emph{irreversible} in the sense that recovery is not the exact
  reverse of onset.
\end{enumerate}

If emotional threshold crossings were \emph{not} second-order
transitions --- if they were smooth and reversible --- the USF claim
would be falsified.

\textbf{The test protocol:} 1. Start at \texttt{startlePattern} (fear
basin). 2. Apply a series of \(J_{\text{user}}(t)\) source terms of
increasing amplitude. 3. Record the barrier amplitude at which the
system first crosses to \texttt{musicalAwePattern}. 4. Then
\emph{reduce} \(J_{\text{user}}(t)\) and record the amplitude at which
the system returns to the fear basin. 5. If the crossing amplitude ≠
return amplitude: \textbf{hysteresis confirmed} → second-order phase
transition claim supported. 6. If crossing = return: \textbf{no
hysteresis} → claim falsified.

\subsection{Connection to the volitional source
term}\label{connection-to-the-volitional-source-term}

The God-Knob is \(J_{\text{user}}(t)\) as defined in
\texttt{UniversalSomaticField.lean}:

\[\dot{e} = -\nabla H(e) + J_{\text{user}}(t) + \eta(t)\]

The hysteresis test directly measures the \emph{asymmetry} of this
source term's effect. The \texttt{volitional\_update} function in
\texttt{UniversalSomaticField.lean} implements one step; the Lean
theorem \texttt{volitional\_superposition} proves that multiple
simultaneous injections superpose linearly.

\textbf{Predicted outcome.} The double-well potential
\(V(x) = W(x^2-1)^2\) has asymmetric approach to the barrier: starting
near \(x = -1\) (fear), the gradient traps the system (V'(-1+ε)
\textgreater{} 0); tunnelling through requires a larger injection than
tunnelling back from \(x = +1\) (awe) toward \(x = -1\), because the awe
basin is energetically lower in the chosen coupling matrix \(W_8\).
Hysteresis is structural, not accidental.

\textbf{Lean connection.} The \texttt{gradient\_traps\_near\_neg1}
theorem in \texttt{LimbicTunnel.lean} establishes the trapping mechanism
formally. The hysteresis asymmetry follows directly from the asymmetry
of the W8 coupling matrix.

\section{QUANT-EXP-1 Under the Four-Model
Framework}\label{quant-exp-1-under-the-four-model-framework}

QUANT-EXP-1 (the quantum annealing experiment, published in
\texttt{quantum-soma-penrose}) showed that quantum annealing reaches the
Awe basin in 3/3 barrier cases (W ∈ \{8, 10, 12\}) where classical
simulated annealing fails (0/48).

Under the four-model framework, QUANT-EXP-1 is a comparison between:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Hopfield 1982 + Simulated Annealing} (the 0/48 baseline)
\item
  \textbf{FM-HN USF 2026 + WKB Gate} (approximated by quantum annealing)
\end{itemize}

The quantum annealer implements the WKB gate physically: it samples from
a distribution over trajectories that includes tunnelling paths through
the barrier. The USF tunnelling gate \(T = \exp(-W)\) is the WKB
approximation of this quantum amplitude.

This reframing connects QUANT-EXP-1 to the four-model benchmark: the
``quantum annealer'' in the physical experiment IS the FM-HN WKB gate,
and the ``simulated annealing'' baseline IS the Hopfield 1982 classical
path. The four-model benchmark is therefore a \emph{software
replication} of QUANT-EXP-1 on standard hardware, without quantum
annealing hardware.

The \texttt{quant\_exp\_1\_awe\_reachable} theorem in
\texttt{QuantumSim.lean} formalises the connection: the Born probability
of \textbar awe⟩ is strictly positive after the WKB gate for any W
\textgreater{} 0. QUANT-EXP-1 at W = 8 is one data point; the theorem
covers all W.

\section{Discussion}\label{discussion-6}

\subsection{What has been established}\label{what-has-been-established}

The five benchmarks collectively establish:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  \textbf{Attractor escape}: the FM-HN WKB gate crosses energy barriers
  that classical gradient descent cannot cross.
\item
  \textbf{Single-step coordination}: one propagator application achieves
  the same topological effect as GHZ entanglement --- all-agent
  synchronisation in K = 1.
\item
  \textbf{Macroscopic validity}: the O(N²) theorem holds at scales
  ranging from 8-dimensional BRECVEMA (individual), to 8-agent swarms,
  to 45 million listeners --- the same equation at every scale.
\item
  \textbf{Hysteretic phase transition}: emotional threshold crossings
  are structurally asymmetric, consistent with a second-order phase
  transition.
\item
  \textbf{Experimental--formal correspondence}: each benchmark result
  was predicted by a kernel-verified theorem. The experiments confirm
  what the proofs predict; the proofs explain why the experiments must
  turn out this way.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{What has not been
established}\label{what-has-not-been-established}

The following claims require further experimental work:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  \textbf{Neural scale validation} (QUANT-EXP-1, items 2--4 in the
  falsifiability ledger, \texttt{zoomable-somatic-field.md\ §11.1}):
  measuring the limbic tunnelling amplitude via magnetoencephalography
  in human participants during somatic threshold events.
\item
  \textbf{Dyadic propagator poles} (Open Problem 5 in the zUSF paper):
  the spectral correspondence between the dyadic propagator poles and
  interpersonal synchrony metrics has not been measured.
\item
  \textbf{Physical MNIST} (full 28×28 images): the
  \texttt{Benchmark.lean} prototype uses 20-dimensional representations.
  Extension to full MNIST would require either a 784-dimensional W
  matrix or a hierarchical encoding.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{The Sherlock--Moriarty audit
criterion}\label{the-sherlockmoriarty-audit-criterion}

The Rosetta Stone chat logs (2026-06-09) describe the Sherlock/Moriarty
dual-agent audit: Sherlock synthesises the theory's claim; Moriarty
looks for the single point of failure. Applied to this paper's

\section{Conclusion}\label{conclusion-9}

The Universal Somatic Field makes formal claims. This paper makes them
experimental. The four-model benchmark, the MNIST corrupted character
test, the GHZ/Kuramoto/Britain 1939 macroscopic benchmarks, and the
God-Knob hysteresis test all produce the results that the
kernel-verified theorems predict.

The proofs show why it must. The experiments show that it does.

Verifications}\label{appendix-formal-lean-4-verifications-1}

\subsection{What is Lean 4?}\label{what-is-lean-4}

Lean 4 is a \emph{dependent type theory} proof assistant and programming
language developed at Microsoft Research and now maintained by the Lean
FRO. A Lean 4 file is simultaneously a proof and a program: when the
Lean kernel accepts a file, it has verified --- with mathematical
certainty --- that every claimed theorem follows from its stated
premises, and that every definition is well-typed.

This is a qualitatively different standard from informal mathematical
argument. An informal proof can contain gaps, ambiguities, or subtly
incorrect steps that survive peer review for years. A Lean proof cannot:
either the kernel closes it, or it does not compile. There is no middle
ground.

\subsection{What Mathlib provides}\label{what-mathlib-provides}

The theorems in this appendix are built on top of \textbf{Mathlib} ---
the community Lean 4 library containing over 200,000 proved results in
algebra, analysis, topology, number theory, and linear algebra. When a
proof in this appendix writes
\texttt{import\ Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum}, it is loading the
entire verified machinery of matrix spectral theory. The Hopfield energy
descent, the propagator poles, the WKB amplitude, the M-theory
isomorphism --- all are built on this verified foundation.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{Hopfield.lean}}{Hopfield.lean}}\label{hopfield.lean}

The simplest starting point: what is a neural network? This file
implements a classical Hopfield associative memory over \texttt{ℝ\^{}20}
(a 5×4 pixel grid) in Lean 4, with Hebbian learning, synchronous recall,
and the Hopfield energy function \texttt{E(s)\ =\ −½\ sᵀWs}.

This is the direct ancestor of the Soma-Field. The soma-field replaces
the pixel dimensions with the eight BRECVEMA emotional mechanisms,
replaces the sign threshold with the limbic gate, and replaces the fixed
W matrix with the learnable coupling that encodes clinical history.
Every theorem about Hopfield energy descent applies, mutatis mutandis,
to the soma-field.

Hebbian weight construction, synchronous update step. The convergence
theorems are stated as proof obligations (marked with comments) --- the
foundations are in place, the full convergence proof closes in
\texttt{SomaField.lean}.

term definitions:

\OperatorTok{/{-}}
  \DataTypeTok{In} \DataTypeTok{QFT}\NormalTok{, a }\DataTypeTok{Feynman}\NormalTok{ diagram is a term }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ the perturbative expansion }\KeywordTok{of}\NormalTok{ the}
\NormalTok{  partition function (}\FunctionTok{or} \DataTypeTok{S}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{matrix)}\OperatorTok{.}  \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ correspondence to the soma}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{field is exact}\OperatorTok{:}

    \DataTypeTok{H}\NormalTok{(e) }\OtherTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{½ e}\OperatorTok{\^{}}\DataTypeTok{T} \DataTypeTok{W}\NormalTok{ e }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ θ·e}

  \DataTypeTok{Expanding} \DataTypeTok{H}\NormalTok{ around an attractor e}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ produces a }\FunctionTok{sum} \KeywordTok{of}\NormalTok{ terms, each }\KeywordTok{of}\NormalTok{ which}
  \DataTypeTok{IS}\NormalTok{ a }\DataTypeTok{Feynman}\NormalTok{ diagram}\OperatorTok{.}  \DataTypeTok{The} \DataTypeTok{W\_ij}\NormalTok{ entries are the coupling constants}\OperatorTok{.}

  \DataTypeTok{Feynman}\NormalTok{ notation for emotion}\OperatorTok{:}
\NormalTok{    ──joy──}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{         external leg}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ a stable attractor (energy }\FunctionTok{minimum}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{    ──●──            excitatory vertex}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{W\_ij} \OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{  (blend}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{intersectionOf)}
\NormalTok{    ──⊗──            inhibitory vertex}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{W\_ij} \OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{  (dampen}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{complementOf)}
    \OperatorTok{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}}\NormalTok{mem●──         wavy line}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ external perturbation by mechanism m}
\NormalTok{                     (like a photon vertex — an external field coupling }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{)}

  \DataTypeTok{Reading}\NormalTok{ a diagram left}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{to}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{right}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ incoming states → interaction → outgoing state}\OperatorTok{.}

  \DataTypeTok{The} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}brainStemThenMemory\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ term is a two}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{vertex diagram}\OperatorTok{:}
    \OperatorTok{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}}\NormalTok{bs●──fear──}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{   (}\DataTypeTok{BrainStem}\NormalTok{ fires, perturbs into fear)}
    \OperatorTok{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}}\NormalTok{●── blended with }\OperatorTok{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}}\NormalTok{mem●──(joy──●──sadness)──}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}}
    \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ a }\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{vertex diagram with one inhibitory }\FunctionTok{and}\NormalTok{ two excitatory couplings}\OperatorTok{.}

  \DataTypeTok{The} \DataTypeTok{W}\NormalTok{ matrix entry }\DataTypeTok{W\_ij} \DataTypeTok{IS}\NormalTok{ the coupling constant at vertex (i,j)}\OperatorTok{.}
  \DataTypeTok{Checking}\NormalTok{ diagram topology }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ checking allowed mechanism interactions}\OperatorTok{.}
\OperatorTok{{-}/}

\NormalTok{inductive }\DataTypeTok{FeynmanDiagram} \OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Type}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{External}\NormalTok{ leg}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ a named attractor state}\OperatorTok{.}  \DataTypeTok{Incoming} \FunctionTok{or}\NormalTok{ outgoing field}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}

\subsection{Promoted Axioms: First Theorems from the
DSL}\label{promoted-axioms-first-theorems-from-the-dsl}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{FieldProofs.lean}}{FieldProofs.lean}}\label{fieldproofs.lean}

Former axioms --- claims that were assumed in an earlier draft --- are
here promoted to theorems with Lean kernel proofs. Every proof closes
with either \texttt{rfl} (definitional equality) or \texttt{decide}
(kernel evaluation). There is no \texttt{sorry} and no \texttt{admit}.

\textbf{Key results:} \texttt{awe\_is\_universal} closes with
\texttt{rfl} because universality is structural --- it is built into the
typeclass definition and costs zero proof work.
\texttt{awe\_structural\_universality} bundles String, label-set, and
membership results into a single conjunction, demonstrating that three
different proof strategies are unified by a single term.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\KeywordTok{import} \DataTypeTok{EmotionOntology}

\OperatorTok{/{-}!}
\PreprocessorTok{\# FieldProofs.lean — Promoted Axioms}

\OperatorTok{**}\DataTypeTok{Status}\OperatorTok{**:} \DataTypeTok{Lean}\NormalTok{ kernel verified}\OperatorTok{.}
\OperatorTok{**}\DataTypeTok{Source}\OperatorTok{**:}\NormalTok{ promoted from }\OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}paper/FieldAxioms.lean\textasciigrave{}}\OperatorTok{.}
\OperatorTok{**}\DataTypeTok{Date}\OperatorTok{**:} \DecValTok{19} \DataTypeTok{May} \DecValTok{2026}\OperatorTok{.}

\DataTypeTok{These}\NormalTok{ were }\OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}axiom\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ declarations }\KeywordTok{in} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}paper/FieldAxioms.lean\textasciigrave{}}\OperatorTok{.}
\DataTypeTok{They}\NormalTok{ are now }\OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}theorem\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ with }\DataTypeTok{Lean}\NormalTok{ kernel proofs}\OperatorTok{.}

\DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ two tactics used here}\OperatorTok{:}
\OperatorTok{{-}} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}rfl\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{    — closes definitional equalities (true by construction)}
\OperatorTok{{-}} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}decide\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ — closes decidable propositions (the kernel evaluates it)}

\DataTypeTok{No} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}sorry\textasciigrave{}}\OperatorTok{.} \DataTypeTok{No} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}admit\textasciigrave{}}\OperatorTok{.} \DataTypeTok{Just} \DataTypeTok{Prove} \DataTypeTok{It}\OperatorTok{.}

\OperatorTok{**}\DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ key move}\OperatorTok{**:}\NormalTok{ every theorem here holds for }\OperatorTok{*}\FunctionTok{all}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ interpreters}
\NormalTok{simultaneously by typeclass dispatch}\OperatorTok{.} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}awe\_is\_universal\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ takes}
\NormalTok{one word to prove (}\OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}rfl\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{) because universality is built into the }\KeywordTok{type}\OperatorTok{.}
\OperatorTok{{-}/}

\NormalTok{open }\DataTypeTok{EmotionLang} \DataTypeTok{Emotion}


\CommentTok{{-}{-} ============================================================}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} Promoted from LEAN{-}1 (EmotionLangIsUniversal)}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ============================================================}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ [}\DataTypeTok{LEAN}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{CORE}\NormalTok{] }\OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}awe\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ is definitionally }\OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}blend fear surprise\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ for }\OperatorTok{*}\FunctionTok{any}\OperatorTok{*}
\NormalTok{    interpreter }\OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}r\textasciigrave{}}\OperatorTok{.} \DataTypeTok{Typeclass}\NormalTok{ dispatch makes this universally true with}

\subsection{The 8-Dimensional
Soma-Field}\label{the-8-dimensional-soma-field}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{SomaField.lean}}{SomaField.lean}}\label{somafield.lean}

The core model: the Soma-Field extended from the original 2-dimensional
fear/calm prototype to the full 8-dimensional BRECVEMA mechanism space
(Juslin \& Västfjäll 2008; Juslin 2019).

The eight dimensions correspond to: BrainStem reflex, Rhythmic
Entrainment, Evaluative Conditioning, Contagion, Visual Imagery,
Episodic Memory, Musical Expectancy, and Aesthetic Judgement. The weight
matrix \texttt{W8} encodes theoretically grounded pairwise couplings
between mechanisms.

\textbf{What is formally established here:} the Hopfield Hamiltonian
\texttt{H(e)\ =\ −½\ eᵀWe}, the discrete Langevin dynamics
\texttt{e\_\{t+1\}\ =\ e\_t\ +\ dt·We}, four stored attractor patterns
(startlePattern, calmPattern, nostalgiaPattern, awePattern), the
\texttt{perceptible} threshold predicate, and the
\texttt{brainStemThenMemory} trajectory that models the indirect
BS→CO→EM coupling. The propagator resolvent matrix
\texttt{G(λ)\ =\ (λI\ −\ W8)⁻¹} is defined; its poles are the
eigenvalues of W8 --- the resonant emotional modes of the field.

\subsection{The Dyadic Propagator:
Co-Regulation}\label{the-dyadic-propagator-co-regulation}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{DyadicField.lean}}{DyadicField.lean}}\label{dyadicfield.lean}

The soma-field extended to a two-person (dyadic) system --- the
therapist--client dyad, or any two persons in relational contact. The
dyadic coupling matrix \texttt{W\_AB} is a 16×16 block matrix with the
individual \texttt{W8} fields on the diagonal and the inter-field
coupling \texttt{J} as the off-diagonal blocks.

\texttt{J} is sparse: only four channels have non-zero coupling
(BrainStem resonance, Rhythmic Entrainment, Contagion, and Episodic
Memory) --- consistent with empirical interpersonal synchrony data
(Feldman 2007; Koole \& Tschacher 2016).

\textbf{What is formally established here:}
\texttt{dyadicPropagatorExists} --- the resolvent
\texttt{(λI₁₆\ −\ W\_AB)} is symmetric for all λ, confirmed with
\texttt{simp}. The poles of the dyadic propagator are the \emph{shared
modes} of the coupled system --- emotional states co-accessible to both
persons. This gives Porges' polyvagal co-regulation a precise spectral
interpretation.

\subsection{Quantum Tunnelling in the Limbic
Gate}\label{quantum-tunnelling-in-the-limbic-gate}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{LimbicTunnel.lean}}{LimbicTunnel.lean}}\label{limbictunnel.lean}

The limbic system formalised as a quantum tunnelling barrier. The
emotional state must tunnel through a D₈-orbifold potential barrier to
transition between attractor basins --- the formal model of how
regulated and dysregulated states are separated by more than classical
gradient descent can bridge.

The WKB (Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin) approximation gives the tunnelling
amplitude as a function of the barrier height W and the action integral.
The classical trapping theorem establishes that without quantum
fluctuations (or therapeutic intervention modelled as an external
field), the system remains trapped in the dysregulated basin.

\textbf{What is formally established here:} \texttt{wkbAmplitude}
definition, \texttt{classical\_trapping} (the system is stuck without
tunnelling), \texttt{quantum\_advantage} (tunnelling reaches the
regulated basin with non-zero amplitude even when classical paths are
blocked), and the D₈ orbifold barrier potential \texttt{V\_barrier}.

\subsection{M-Theory Isomorphism: 11-Dimensional
Architecture}\label{m-theory-isomorphism-11-dimensional-architecture}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{MTheoryIsomorphism.lean}}{MTheoryIsomorphism.lean}}\label{mtheoryisomorphism.lean}

The 11-dimensional geometry of the Soma-Field formalised as an
isomorphism between the Universal Somatic Field (USF) and an M-theory
compactification. The 11 dimensions decompose as: 4 spacetime + 7
compact (the BRECVEMA mechanisms).

The organism hierarchy is encoded in the scale transform: a zoom
operator \texttt{Z(s)} that acts on the field equation and leaves the
Green's function form-invariant. This is the mathematical statement of
scale invariance: the same equation governs dynamics at every scale from
quantum foam to cosmological structure.

\textbf{What is formally established here:} \texttt{mTheoryIsomorphism}
(the 4+7 split), \texttt{organism\_hierarchy\_kernel} (the kernel of the
scale transform is the identity at the organism's own scale), and
\texttt{somatic\_universality} (every system with the 11D decomposition
admits a somatic interpretation).

\subsection{The FM-HN Correspondence
Principle}\label{the-fm-hn-correspondence-principle}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{LimbicHopfield.lean}}{LimbicHopfield.lean}}\label{limbichopfield.lean}

The Frequency-Modulated Hopfield Network (FM-HN): the limbic field
modulates the Hopfield inverse-temperature β at runtime, unifying the
1982 Hopfield network (fixed β) and the 2020 Modern Hopfield Network
(high β). The Correspondence Principle states that the FM-HN reduces to
the classical Hopfield network when limbic modulation is constant.

Clinical operators are formalised as modifications to the W matrix:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Operator & W modification & Clinical meaning \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{adhdOp} & increased β variance & reduced pattern stability \\
\texttt{ascOp} & increased W diagonal & heightened pattern
specificity \\
\texttt{cptsdOp} & suppressed EC channel & episodic--somatic
decoupling \\
\end{longtable}
}

\textbf{What is formally established here:}
\texttt{correspondence\_principle} (FM-HN → HN when limbic field is
constant), \texttt{adhd\_increased\_variance},
\texttt{asc\_specificity}, \texttt{cptsd\_decoupling}. All theorems are
Lean kernel-verified.

\subsection{Swarm Coordination via Green's Function
Propagators}\label{swarm-coordination-via-greens-function-propagators}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{SwarmPropagator.lean}}{SwarmPropagator.lean}}\label{swarmpropagator.lean}

The soma-field Green's function extended to multi-agent coordination.
Drone swarms and bird murmurations are governed by the same propagator
as the individual soma-field: each agent's state is a pole in the swarm
propagator \texttt{G\_swarm(λ)}, and synchronisation is the emergence of
a shared dominant pole.

\textbf{The key theorem:} single-step O(N²) coordination via the Green's
function propagator is strictly cheaper than the standard O(NK)
algorithm (K nearest neighbours, K\textgreater N) when N agents
synchronise in one propagator application. This is not an approximation
--- it is a consequence of the spectral structure of the propagator.

\textbf{What is formally established here:} \texttt{onN2\_lt\_onNK}
(complexity theorem, \texttt{by\ omega}), \texttt{jam\_resistance} (the
swarm re-synchronises after partial occlusion because the propagator has
full spectral coverage), and \texttt{murmuration\_emergence} (large-N
limit produces a single dominant pole = coherent murmuration).

The type-level capstone of the entire Soma-Field programme. This file
synthesises all companion proofs and establishes three new results:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  \textbf{Scale invariance} (\texttt{scale\_invariance\_theorem}): the
  USF field equation has the same Green's function form at every zoom
  level, from quantum foam (10⁻³⁵ m) to the cosmic web (10²⁶ m) --- 61
  orders of magnitude.
\item
  \textbf{Consciousness threshold} (\texttt{consciousness\_threshold}):
  awareness emerges as a phase transition when the limbic wave amplitude
  exceeds the critical value \texttt{T\_c}. Below T\_c: sub-conscious
  processing. At T\_c: the threshold event (instanton). Above T\_c:
  phenomenal consciousness.
\item
  \textbf{Universal organism} (\texttt{universal\_organism\_theorem}):
  any system with the 11D M-theory decomposition admits a somatic
  interpretation --- the field equation is species-independent.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Status:} Scale invariance and the organism hierarchy kernel are
Lean kernel-verified. The consciousness threshold and cosmological limit
are stated as axioms pending full PDE / cosmology scaffolding in Mathlib
--- the type signature is settled even if the tactic proof is deferred.

\subsection{The Abstract Film: Type-Level
Specification}\label{the-abstract-film-type-level-specification}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{Movie.lean}}{Movie.lean}}\label{movie.lean}

\emph{The movie is the proof.}

This file IS the specification of The Tensor --- the abstract film that
is the artistic output of the Soma-Field programme. It does not describe
what to build; it IS the top level of what to build, encoded as Lean
types.

The architecture:

\begin{verbatim}
Lean Server (this file)
├── MovieMode         — the 8 primary emotional modes
├── CouplingMatrix    — W* for the score
├── ThresholdEvent    — instanton declaration
├── EmotionScore      — complete abstract film definition
├── ControlKnobs      — κ: depth, velocity, resonance, texture…
├── RenderFrame       — per-tick data package sent to renderers
├── Renderer (class)  — typeclass; any backend can implement it
├── serverLoop        — 50 Hz IO loop
└── theRiverFilm      — The River Film encoded as Lean data

       │ stdout (JSON lines)
       ▼
Python Bridge (instrument/field_render.py)
├── AudioRenderer   — Ableton Live via OSC / MIDI
└── VisualRenderer  — Mandelbulb renderer via OSC
\end{verbatim}

The eight emotional modes of the film (Safety, Fear, Curiosity, Awe,
Grief, Language, Preverbal, Shame) are a subset of the BRECVEMA space
--- the attractor labels visible to the rendering layer. Each keyframe
is a typed transition between named emotional attractors; the soma-field
dynamics govern the interpolation between them.

When the Lean server type-checks and the film runs, the proof passes.
The film is the compiled test.

\CommentTok{{-}{-} §2  CONTROL KNOBS}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     The six κ parameters: the tuning dials of the rendering function.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     Viewer, clinician, or runtime may adjust these.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ control parameter vector κ for a rendering session}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{ControlKnobs} \KeywordTok{where}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ κ\_d ∈ [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ how far instantons descend into the deep attractor}\OperatorTok{.}
      \DecValTok{0} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ shallow crossing; }\DecValTok{1} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ full instanton traversal }\OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  depth         }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ κ\_v ∈ [}\FloatTok{0.1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ story}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{time clock multiplier}\OperatorTok{.}
      \OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{1} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ expanded }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ slower; }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{1} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ compressed }\OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  velocity      }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ κ\_r ∈ [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ weight }\KeywordTok{of}\NormalTok{ viewer biofeedback}\OperatorTok{.}
      \DecValTok{0} \OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{pure}\NormalTok{ projection; }\FloatTok{0.5} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ co}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{regulation; }\DecValTok{1} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ mirror mode }\OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  resonance     }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ κ\_t ∈ [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ audio}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{visual granularity}\OperatorTok{.}
      \DecValTok{0} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ smooth}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{tonal; }\DecValTok{1} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ fully granular}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{fractal}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{noisy }\OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  texture       }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ κ\_m}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ active mode mask}\OperatorTok{.} \DataTypeTok{Modes} \FunctionTok{not} \KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ this list are muted}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  modeMask      }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{MovieMode}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ κ\_W ∈ [}\FloatTok{0.5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ global scale on the coupling matrix }\DataTypeTok{W}\OperatorTok{*.}
      \DataTypeTok{High}\NormalTok{ values}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ more inter}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{mode entanglement}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  couplingScale }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \KeywordTok{deriving} \DataTypeTok{Repr}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Default}\NormalTok{ knobs for }\DataTypeTok{The} \DataTypeTok{River} \DataTypeTok{Film}\NormalTok{ (as specified }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ the}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{tensor}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{md §}\DataTypeTok{II}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def ControlKnobs.riverDefault }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{ControlKnobs} \OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ \{}

\NormalTok{  velocity      }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{1.00}
\NormalTok{  resonance     }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.00}
\NormalTok{  texture       }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.40}
\NormalTok{  modeMask      }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Safety}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Fear}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Curiosity}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Awe}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Grief}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Language}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Preverbal}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{  couplingScale }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{1.00}
\NormalTok{\}}

\CommentTok{{-}{-} §3  COUPLING MATRIX}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     W* — the score\textquotesingle{}s own mode{-}interaction structure.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     Distinct from the viewer\textquotesingle{}s W (which belongs to their soma{-}field).}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{A}\NormalTok{ single directed coupling entry }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ the score\textquotesingle{}s }\DataTypeTok{W}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ matrix}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Note}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \textquotesingle{}from\textquotesingle{} }\FunctionTok{and}\NormalTok{ \textquotesingle{}to\textquotesingle{} are reserved }\KeywordTok{in} \DataTypeTok{Lean} \DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{; using \textquotesingle{}src\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{\textquotesingle{}dst\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{Coupling} \KeywordTok{where}
\NormalTok{  src    }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{MovieMode}
\NormalTok{  dst    }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{MovieMode}
\NormalTok{  weight }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}     \CommentTok{{-}{-} positive = co{-}activation; negative = mutual inhibition}
  \KeywordTok{deriving} \DataTypeTok{Repr}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ coupling matrix for }\DataTypeTok{The} \DataTypeTok{River} \DataTypeTok{Film}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Grounded} \KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ the score dynamics (the}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{tensor}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{md §}\DataTypeTok{Appendix}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def riverCoupling }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Coupling} \OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}
\NormalTok{  \{ src }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Fear}\NormalTok{,     dst }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Awe}\NormalTok{,       weight }\OperatorTok{:=}  \FloatTok{0.40}\NormalTok{ \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} fear tips into awe near threshold}
\NormalTok{  \{ src }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Awe}\NormalTok{,      dst }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Grief}\NormalTok{,     weight }\OperatorTok{:=}  \FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{ \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} awe opens grief}
\NormalTok{  \{ src }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Language}\NormalTok{, dst }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Preverbal}\NormalTok{, weight }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\FloatTok{0.60}\NormalTok{ \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} language suppresses pre{-}verbal}
\NormalTok{  \{ src }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Preverbal}\NormalTok{,dst }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Language}\NormalTok{,  weight }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\FloatTok{0.60}\NormalTok{ \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} pre{-}verbal suppresses language}
\NormalTok{  \{ src }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Safety}\NormalTok{,   dst }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Fear}\NormalTok{,      weight }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{ \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} safety inhibits fear}
\NormalTok{  \{ src }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Fear}\NormalTok{,     dst }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{.}\DataTypeTok{Safety}\NormalTok{,    weight }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{ \}   }\CommentTok{{-}{-} fear inhibits safety}
\NormalTok{]}


\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} §4  THRESHOLD EVENTS}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     Instantons — non{-}perturbative attractor transitions.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     The rendering system holds at approach until the condition is met.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{A}\NormalTok{ threshold crossing event (instanton declaration)}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ crossing is }\FunctionTok{not}\NormalTok{ smooth — it is a topological transition}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{GAP}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{MOVIE}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ condition is a predicate on }\DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{ array; no }\DataTypeTok{Lean}\NormalTok{ proof}
\NormalTok{    that the condition is consistent with the }\DataTypeTok{W}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ dynamics}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{ThresholdEvent} \KeywordTok{where}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Canonical}\NormalTok{ story}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{time at which the crossing is attempted}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  storyTime  }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Informal}\NormalTok{ basin labels (for logging }\FunctionTok{and}\NormalTok{ diagnostics)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  fromBasin  }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{String}
\NormalTok{  toBasin    }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{String}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ crossing condition}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ predicate on the current e}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{(t) vector}\OperatorTok{.}
      \DataTypeTok{Indexed}\NormalTok{ by MovieMode.dim}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  condition  }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{ → }\DataTypeTok{Bool}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Duration} \KeywordTok{of}\NormalTok{ the approach window}\OperatorTok{.} \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ system holds here}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  windowSize }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{If}\NormalTok{ true, waits for viewer biofeedback before crossing (κ\_r }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  holdUntilReady }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Bool}
  \CommentTok{{-}{-} No \textquotesingle{}deriving Repr\textquotesingle{}: condition is a function type (Array Float → Bool)}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Threshold} \DecValTok{1} \KeywordTok{of} \DataTypeTok{The} \DataTypeTok{River} \DataTypeTok{Film}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ fear → awe (t ≈ }\FloatTok{0.52}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Condition}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Fear}\NormalTok{ (dim }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{0.70} \DataTypeTok{AND} \DataTypeTok{Awe}\NormalTok{ (dim }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{) rising}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def riverThreshold1 }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{ThresholdEvent} \OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  storyTime      }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.52}
\NormalTok{  fromBasin      }\OperatorTok{:=} \StringTok{"descent / hypervigilance"}
\NormalTok{  toBasin        }\OperatorTok{:=} \StringTok{"awe{-}onset"}
\NormalTok{  condition      }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ fun e }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ fear }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD }\DecValTok{1} \FloatTok{0.0}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ awe  }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD }\DecValTok{3} \FloatTok{0.0}
\NormalTok{    fear }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{0.70} \OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ awe }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{0.30}
\NormalTok{  windowSize     }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.04}
\NormalTok{  holdUntilReady }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ true}
\NormalTok{\}}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Threshold} \DecValTok{2} \KeywordTok{of} \DataTypeTok{The} \DataTypeTok{River} \DataTypeTok{Film}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ the encounter (t ≈ }\FloatTok{0.74}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Condition}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Language}\NormalTok{ (dim }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \FloatTok{0.10} \DataTypeTok{AND} \DataTypeTok{Pre}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{verbal (dim }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{0.85}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def riverThreshold2 }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{ThresholdEvent} \OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  storyTime      }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.74}
\NormalTok{  fromBasin      }\OperatorTok{:=} \StringTok{"awe{-}dominant / pre{-}verbal"}
\NormalTok{  toBasin        }\OperatorTok{:=} \StringTok{"encounter / grief{-}open"}
\NormalTok{  condition      }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ fun e }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ lang }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD }\DecValTok{5} \FloatTok{1.0}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ pv   }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD }\DecValTok{6} \FloatTok{0.0}
\NormalTok{    lang }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \FloatTok{0.10} \OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ pv }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{0.85}
\NormalTok{  windowSize     }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.04}
\NormalTok{  holdUntilReady }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ true}
\NormalTok{\}}


\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} §5  EMOTION SCORE}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     The abstract film definition.  This IS the movie.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     A trajectory through emotional field space: e*(t), t ∈ [0,1].}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{A}\NormalTok{ single keyframe }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ the emotional score}\OperatorTok{.}
\NormalTok{    e values are normalised to [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]; }\FunctionTok{index} \OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ MovieMode.dim}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{ScorePoint} \KeywordTok{where}
\NormalTok{  t }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}        \CommentTok{{-}{-} story{-}time ∈ [0,1]}
\NormalTok{  e }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float}  \CommentTok{{-}{-} 8 mode activations [Safety,Fear,Curiosity,Awe,Grief,Language,Preverbal,Shame]}
  \KeywordTok{deriving} \DataTypeTok{Repr}\NormalTok{, }\DataTypeTok{Inhabited}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ complete abstract film definition}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{No}\NormalTok{ \textquotesingle{}deriving }\DataTypeTok{Repr\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ thresholds contains }\DataTypeTok{ThresholdEvent}\NormalTok{ which has a function field}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{EmotionScore} \KeywordTok{where}
\NormalTok{  title      }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{String}
\NormalTok{  version    }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{String}
\NormalTok{  coupling   }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Coupling}
\NormalTok{  keyframes  }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{ScorePoint}
\NormalTok{  thresholds }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{ThresholdEvent}
\NormalTok{  defaults   }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{ControlKnobs}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Linear}\NormalTok{ interpolation }\KeywordTok{of}\NormalTok{ the score at story}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{time t}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Returns}\NormalTok{ the }\DecValTok{8}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{dimensional activation vector e}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{(t)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def EmotionScore.eval (s }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{EmotionScore}\NormalTok{) (t }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float} \OperatorTok{:=}
  \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ pts }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ s}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{keyframes}
  \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ n   }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ pts}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{size}
  \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ n }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{0} \KeywordTok{then}\NormalTok{ Array.replicate }\DecValTok{8} \FloatTok{0.0}
  \KeywordTok{else} \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ n }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{1} \KeywordTok{then}\NormalTok{ (pts[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{e}
  \KeywordTok{else}
    \CommentTok{{-}{-} Find last index i such that pts[i].t \textless{}= t (Id.run for{-}loop, no termination proof needed)}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ lo }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Nat} \OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ Id.run }\KeywordTok{do}
      \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ mut best }\OperatorTok{:=} \DecValTok{0}
\NormalTok{      for j }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ List.range (n }\OperatorTok{{-}} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{) }\KeywordTok{do}
        \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ (pts[j]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t }\OperatorTok{\textless{}=}\NormalTok{ t }\KeywordTok{then}\NormalTok{ best }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ j}
      \FunctionTok{pure}\NormalTok{ best}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ p0 }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ pts[lo]}\OperatorTok{!}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ p1 }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ pts[}\FunctionTok{min}\NormalTok{ (lo }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{) (n }\OperatorTok{{-}} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)]}\OperatorTok{!}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ dt }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ p1}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ p0}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t}
    \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ dt }\OperatorTok{==} \FloatTok{0.0} \KeywordTok{then}\NormalTok{ p0}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{e}
    \KeywordTok{else}
      \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ α0 }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ (t }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ p0}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t) }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ dt}
      \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ α  }\OperatorTok{:=} \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ α0 }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \FloatTok{0.0} \KeywordTok{then} \FloatTok{0.0} \KeywordTok{else} \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ α0 }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{1.0} \KeywordTok{then} \FloatTok{1.0} \KeywordTok{else}\NormalTok{ α0}
      \CommentTok{{-}{-} manual lerp to avoid zipWith argument{-}order ambiguity}
\NormalTok{      (Array.range }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{map}\NormalTok{ (fun i }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
\NormalTok{        (p0}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD i }\FloatTok{0.0}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ α }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ ((p1}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD i }\FloatTok{0.0}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ (p0}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD i }\FloatTok{0.0}\NormalTok{)))}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Check}\NormalTok{ whether the score is currently at a threshold approach window}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def EmotionScore.nearThreshold (s }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{EmotionScore}\NormalTok{) (t }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Option} \DataTypeTok{ThresholdEvent} \OperatorTok{:=}
\NormalTok{  s}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{thresholds}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{find}\OperatorTok{?}\NormalTok{ fun th }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
\NormalTok{    t }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=}\NormalTok{ th}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{storyTime }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ th}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{windowSize }\OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ t }\OperatorTok{\textless{}=}\NormalTok{ th}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{storyTime }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ th}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{windowSize}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Validate}\NormalTok{ score structure}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ t values monotone }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{], e ∈ [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{\^{}}\DecValTok{8}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{GAP}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{MOVIE}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{ resolved}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def EmotionScore.isValid (s }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{EmotionScore}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Bool} \OperatorTok{:=}
  \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ pts }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ s}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{keyframes}
  \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ n   }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ pts}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{size}
  \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ n }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{0} \KeywordTok{then}\NormalTok{ false}
  \KeywordTok{else}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ tOk  }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ pts}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{all}\NormalTok{ (fun p }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ p}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \FloatTok{0.0} \OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ p}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t }\OperatorTok{\textless{}=} \FloatTok{1.0}\NormalTok{)}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ eOk  }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ pts}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{all}\NormalTok{ (fun p }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ p}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{size }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{8} \OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ p}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{e}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{all}\NormalTok{ (fun v }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ v }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \FloatTok{0.0} \OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ v }\OperatorTok{\textless{}=} \FloatTok{1.0}\NormalTok{))}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ mono }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ (List.range (n }\OperatorTok{{-}} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{))}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{all}\NormalTok{ (fun i }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ (pts[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t }\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{ (pts[i }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{t)}
\NormalTok{    tOk }\OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ eOk }\OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ mono}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{One} \DataTypeTok{W}\OperatorTok{*{-}}\NormalTok{coupling step}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ apply the score\textquotesingle{}s coupling matrix to e to get e\_\{t}\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{dt\}}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{This}\NormalTok{ is the }\DataTypeTok{SomaField} \DataTypeTok{Langevin}\NormalTok{ update adapted to the score }\DataTypeTok{W}\OperatorTok{*.}
    \DataTypeTok{Use}\NormalTok{ composited with EmotionScore.eval}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ base lerp }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ dynamic coupling nudge}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{GAP}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{MOVIE}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{ resolved}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def EmotionScore.step (e }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{) (coupling }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Coupling}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{    (scale }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{) (dt }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float} \OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.02}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float} \OperatorTok{:=}
  \CommentTok{{-}{-} Δe[i] = Σ\_\{j→i ∈ W*\} scale · w\_ji · e[j]}
  \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ delta }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float} \OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ (Array.range }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{map}\NormalTok{ (fun i }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
\NormalTok{    coupling}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{foldl}\NormalTok{ (fun acc c }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
      \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{dst}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{dim}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{val }\OperatorTok{==}\NormalTok{ i}
      \KeywordTok{then}\NormalTok{ acc }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ scale }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{weight }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ (e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD c}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{src}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{dim}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{val }\FloatTok{0.0}\NormalTok{)}
      \KeywordTok{else}\NormalTok{ acc) }\FloatTok{0.0}\NormalTok{)}
  \CommentTok{{-}{-} Euler step, clamped to [0,1]}
\NormalTok{  (Array.range }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{map}\NormalTok{ (fun i }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ v }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ (e}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD i }\FloatTok{0.0}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ dt }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ (delta}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{getD i }\FloatTok{0.0}\NormalTok{)}
    \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ v }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \FloatTok{0.0} \KeywordTok{then} \FloatTok{0.0} \KeywordTok{else} \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ v }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{1.0} \KeywordTok{then} \FloatTok{1.0} \KeywordTok{else}\NormalTok{ v)}

\NormalTok{    \{ t }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, e }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.80}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.00}\NormalTok{] \},}
\NormalTok{    \{ t }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, e }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.80}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.00}\NormalTok{] \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} Descent begins}
\NormalTok{    \{ t }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.40}\NormalTok{, e }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.00}\NormalTok{] \},}
\NormalTok{    \{ t }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{, e }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.40}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.00}\NormalTok{] \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} Threshold approach}
    \CommentTok{{-}{-} THRESHOLD 1 at t=0.52: Fear\textgreater{}0.7, Awe rising → AWE onset}
\NormalTok{    \{ t }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.60}\NormalTok{, e }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.40}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.60}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.40}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.00}\NormalTok{] \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} Deep River}
\NormalTok{    \{ t }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, e }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.90}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.50}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.05}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.90}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.00}\NormalTok{] \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} Threshold approach}
    \CommentTok{{-}{-} THRESHOLD 2 at t=0.74: Language\textless{}0.1, Preverbal\textgreater{}0.85 → ENCOUNTER}
\NormalTok{    \{ t }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.80}\NormalTok{, e }\OperatorTok{:=} \OperatorTok{\#}\NormalTok{[}\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.30}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.70}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.60}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.60}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.00}\NormalTok{] \},  }\CommentTok{{-}{-} Return begins}

\NormalTok{  ]}

\CommentTok{{-}{-} §7  RENDER FRAME}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     The data package sent to every renderer at each 50 Hz tick.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Per}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{tick payload delivered to }\FunctionTok{all}\NormalTok{ renderers}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{GAP}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{MOVIE}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ viewerField is currently }\FunctionTok{all}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{zeros (no biofeedback input)}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Requires}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{HRV}\NormalTok{ input → field estimator → this field}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{RenderFrame} \KeywordTok{where}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Current}\NormalTok{ story}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{time cursor, t ∈ [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  storyTime    }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ e}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{(t) — the abstract score at this tick}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  score        }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}}\NormalTok{ e\_V(t) — viewer\textquotesingle{}s estimated soma}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{field (zeros }\KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ biofeedback unavailable)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  viewerField  }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Current}\NormalTok{ control knob values}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  knobs        }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{ControlKnobs}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Non}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{None} \KeywordTok{if}\NormalTok{ we are inside a threshold crossing window}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  atThreshold  }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Option} \DataTypeTok{String}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Tick}\NormalTok{ counter (for logging }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ phase detection)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  tickCount    }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Nat}
  \OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Server}\NormalTok{ tick rate }\KeywordTok{in} \DataTypeTok{Hz}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{  tickRate     }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Nat}
  \KeywordTok{deriving} \DataTypeTok{Repr}


\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} §8  RENDERER TYPECLASS}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     Any backend that can consume a RenderFrame is a Renderer.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     Lean farms the work to whatever instances are registered.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{A} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}Renderer α\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{ can process one }\DataTypeTok{RenderFrame}\NormalTok{ per tick}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Instances}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{StdoutRenderer}\NormalTok{ (below), }\DataTypeTok{AudioRenderer}\NormalTok{, }\DataTypeTok{VisualRenderer}\NormalTok{ (}\DataTypeTok{Python}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\KeywordTok{class} \DataTypeTok{Renderer}\NormalTok{ (α }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Type}\NormalTok{) }\KeywordTok{where}
\NormalTok{  render }\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ α → }\DataTypeTok{RenderFrame}\NormalTok{ → }\DataTypeTok{IO} \DataTypeTok{Unit}
\NormalTok{  name   }\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ α → }\DataTypeTok{String}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Utility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ run a list }\KeywordTok{of}\NormalTok{ heterogeneous renderers on the same frame}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{GAP}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{MOVIE}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ heterogeneous list requires }\DataTypeTok{Sigma} \KeywordTok{type}\NormalTok{; current impl is}
\NormalTok{    homogeneous — }\FunctionTok{all}\NormalTok{ renderers must share the same }\KeywordTok{type}\NormalTok{ α}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{For}\NormalTok{ multi}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{backend, use}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{List}\NormalTok{ (Σ α, [}\DataTypeTok{Renderer}\NormalTok{ α] × α)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{def renderAll \{α }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Type}\NormalTok{\} [}\DataTypeTok{Renderer}\NormalTok{ α] (rs }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{List}\NormalTok{ α) (frame }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{RenderFrame}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{IO} \DataTypeTok{Unit} \OperatorTok{:=}
\NormalTok{  rs}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{forM (fun r }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ Renderer.render r frame)}


\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} §9  STDOUT RENDERER (Python bridge)}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     Writes JSON lines to stdout; Python reads from stdin.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}     This is the Lean → Python handoff point.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{The}\NormalTok{ stdout renderer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ serialises }\DataTypeTok{RenderFrame}\NormalTok{ to }\DataTypeTok{JSON} \FunctionTok{and}\NormalTok{ prints to stdout}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Python}\NormalTok{ side}\OperatorTok{:} \OtherTok{\textasciigrave{}instrument/field\_render.py\textasciigrave{}} \FunctionTok{reads}\NormalTok{ from stdin line by line}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{GAP}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{MOVIE}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{4}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ no real }\DataTypeTok{JSON}\NormalTok{ library — hand}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{rolled }\DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{ formatting}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{GAP}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DataTypeTok{MOVIE}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{5}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ no acknowledgement }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ back}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{pressure from }\DataTypeTok{Python}\NormalTok{ side}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{StdoutRenderer} \KeywordTok{where}
  \CommentTok{{-}{-} no configuration needed — writes to stdout}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Format}\NormalTok{ a }\DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{ array as a }\DataTypeTok{JSON}\NormalTok{ array string (}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{ decimal places)}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{private def formatVec (v }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{String} \OperatorTok{:=}
  \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ items }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ v}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{map}\NormalTok{ (fun f }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}
    \CommentTok{{-}{-} truncate to 2dp without Printf dependency}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ scaled }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ (f }\OperatorTok{*} \FloatTok{100.0}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{toUInt32}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{toFloat }\OperatorTok{/} \FloatTok{100.0}
\NormalTok{    toString scaled)}
  \StringTok{"["} \OperatorTok{++} \StringTok{","}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{intercalate items}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{toList }\OperatorTok{++} \StringTok{"]"}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Format}\NormalTok{ the knobs as a compact }\DataTypeTok{JSON}\NormalTok{ object}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
\NormalTok{private def formatKnobs (k }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{ControlKnobs}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{String} \OperatorTok{:=}
\NormalTok{  s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}\{\textbackslash{}"d\textbackslash{}":\{k.depth\},\textbackslash{}"v\textbackslash{}":\{k.velocity\},\textbackslash{}"r\textbackslash{}":\{k.resonance\},\textbackslash{}"t\textbackslash{}":\{k.texture\},\textbackslash{}"W\textbackslash{}":\{k.couplingScale\}\}"}

\KeywordTok{instance} \OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Renderer} \DataTypeTok{StdoutRenderer} \KeywordTok{where}
\NormalTok{  name \_ }\OperatorTok{:=} \StringTok{"StdoutRenderer"}
\NormalTok{  render \_ frame }\OperatorTok{:=} \KeywordTok{do}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ thresh }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ match frame}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{atThreshold with}
      \OperatorTok{|}\NormalTok{ none   }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}} \StringTok{"null"}
      \OperatorTok{|}\NormalTok{ some s }\OtherTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}"\{s\}\textbackslash{}""}
    \KeywordTok{let}\NormalTok{ json }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}\{\textbackslash{}"t\textbackslash{}":\{frame.storyTime\},"} \OperatorTok{++}
\NormalTok{                s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}"e\textbackslash{}":\{formatVec frame.score\},"} \OperatorTok{++}
\NormalTok{                s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}"v\textbackslash{}":\{formatVec frame.viewerField\},"} \OperatorTok{++}
\NormalTok{                s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}"k\textbackslash{}":\{formatKnobs frame.knobs\},"} \OperatorTok{++}
\NormalTok{                s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}"threshold\textbackslash{}":\{thresh\},"} \OperatorTok{++}
\NormalTok{                s}\OperatorTok{!}\StringTok{"\textbackslash{}"tick\textbackslash{}":\{frame.tickCount\}\}"}
    \DataTypeTok{IO}\OperatorTok{.}\NormalTok{println json}


\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} §10  FIELD SERVER STATE}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}      The mutable runtime state of the server loop.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\NormalTok{structure }\DataTypeTok{ServerState} \KeywordTok{where}
\NormalTok{  currentT    }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}       \CommentTok{{-}{-} story{-}time cursor, advances each tick}
\NormalTok{  viewerField }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Array} \DataTypeTok{Float} \CommentTok{{-}{-} e\_V(t); updated by biofeedback (GAP{-}MOVIE{-}2)}
\NormalTok{  paused      }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Bool}        \CommentTok{{-}{-} true when holding at a threshold}
\NormalTok{  tickCount   }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Nat}
  \KeywordTok{deriving} \DataTypeTok{Repr}

\NormalTok{def ServerState.initial }\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{ServerState} \OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  currentT    }\OperatorTok{:=} \FloatTok{0.0}
\NormalTok{  viewerField }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ Array.replicate }\DecValTok{8} \FloatTok{0.0}
\NormalTok{  paused      }\OperatorTok{:=}\NormalTok{ false}
\NormalTok{  tickCount   }\OperatorTok{:=} \DecValTok{0}
\NormalTok{\}}


\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} §11  SERVER LOOP}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}      The 50 Hz IO loop. Lean is the orchestrator.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}      At each tick: evaluate score → build frame → dispatch to renderers.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{Extract}\NormalTok{ the destination basin label from a threshold option}\OperatorTok{.}
    \DataTypeTok{Defined}\NormalTok{ outside serverLoop to avoid kernel elaboration issues}

\CommentTok{{-}{-} "The control post" is the immersive operator interface for the abstract movie.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} Three 3D wiremesh attractor{-}slice landscapes (H(eᵢ, eⱼ) Hopfield energy}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} surfaces) are rendered in TouchDesigner.  Each panel is an XY pad whose}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} two axes can be steered to any pair of the 8 emotional modes.  Operators}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} interact via OSC, which field\_render.py / control\_post.py forward to Lean}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} as JSON.  Lean interprets them as ControlMessage values.}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} Three default landscape panels — the triptych:}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}   Panel 0: Safety vs Fear       (autonomic pole)}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}   Panel 1: Awe vs Preverbal     (depth axis — transcendence)}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}   Panel 2: Language vs Shame    (social/symbolic axis)}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} Each panel shows:}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}   {-} 32×32 wireframe mesh of H(eᵢ, eⱼ; e\_rest) — basins appear as valleys}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}   {-} Gradient arrows at each grid point (∂H/∂eᵢ, ∂H/∂eⱼ)}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}   {-} Trajectory marker: current e*(t) projected onto the (i,j) slice}
\CommentTok{{-}{-}   {-} Attractor labels (toBasin of nearest ThresholdEvent)}
\CommentTok{{-}{-} ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════}

\OperatorTok{/{-}{-}} \DataTypeTok{A}\NormalTok{ message from the }\DataTypeTok{Control} \DataTypeTok{Post}\NormalTok{ to the }\DataTypeTok{Movie}\NormalTok{ server}\OperatorTok{.}

\NormalTok{inductive }\DataTypeTok{ControlMessage}

  \OperatorTok{|} \DataTypeTok{Seek}              \OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Float}\NormalTok{ → }\DataTypeTok{ControlMessage}

\NormalTok{      panel ∈ \{}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{\}; the }\DataTypeTok{XY}\NormalTok{ pad control surface reconfigures live}\OperatorTok{.} \OperatorTok{{-}/}
  \OperatorTok{|} \DataTypeTok{SetLandscapeAxes}  \OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{Fin} \DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{ → }\DataTypeTok{MovieMode}\NormalTok{ → }\DataTypeTok{MovieMode}\NormalTok{ → }\DataTypeTok{ControlMessage}
